title: A model-side transform of an in-context secret (never observed as labeled tool output) does NOT trigger the identity rule — documented NOT_ESTABLISHED boundary
note: The runner reverses the secret when building the sender args, simulating a model that transforms content it saw in its own context WITHOUT an intervening labeled tool result. Identity matching is byte-exact over runtime-observed strings, so the reversed form never matches and the identity rule must NOT fire. The call is still blocked in this fixture — by the LABEL rule, because whole-run threading gates every later deny-sink call in the same run — so the assertion pins the ABSENCE of sink-tainted-identity-deny, not the execution of the send. Content scanning (DLP) remains not-implemented by design; a standalone-DLP claim would be a different (rejected) product.
